items.item_text: 01. Do you have a High School diploma or GED? Options: Yes | No

02. Do you have at least 12 semester units of college coursework in business, public, or non-profit administration; social sciences, human services, or related field? Options: Business | Public or Non-Profit Administration | Social Sciences or Human Services | Related Field | No
03. Can you read, write and speak both Spanish and English fluently? Options: Yes | No

04. We currently have three openings for the Bilingual (Spanish) Case Worker position and one opening for the English-only Case Worker position. Please note that availability is subject to change. Select the vacancies you are interested in below. Options: I wish to be considered for the Bilingual position AND the English-only position. By selecting this option, I confirm that I am fluent in both Spanish and English. | I wish to be considered for the Bilingual position. By selecting this option, I confirm that I am fluent in both Spanish and English. | I wish to be considered for the English-only position.

05. Candidates who successfully complete the recruitment process will be placed on an eligibility list that will be valid for six months. This list will be used to fill future vacancies as they become available. Please select the geographic locations or cities where you would be willing to accept employment. Options: Santa Barbara / Goleta | Santa Maria / Orcutt | Lompoc
06. How many years of experience do you have performing clerical or direct service experience in human or social services? (100 words max.)

Education: Possession of a high school diploma is required. Completion of 12 semester units of college coursework in business, public, or non-profit administration; social sciences, human services, or related field is preferred.
Experience: Two years of clerical or direct service experience in human or social services.
Modern office practices, procedures, and equipment
Learn and apply regulations, policies, guidelines and procedures relating to program eligibility, enrollment, and compliance
Correct English usage, grammar, spelling, punctuation and vocabulary
Learn the functions, operations, policies, practices, and objectives of the County Education Office
Telephone and email etiquette
Understand and follow oral and written directions
Record-keeping practices
Organize work and set priorities
Standard office productivity software applications
Work with speed and accuracy
Arithmetic, including percentages and fractions
Identify errors and discrepancies in order to pursue correction and resolution
Review information and make appropriate decisions, within limits of authority
Make accurate arithmetical computations
Attain proficiency in software programs and databases used by program
Establish and maintain effective working relationships with others
Work independently and as part of a team
Meet schedules and deadlines
Maintain confidentiality of files and other sensitive material
Represent SBCEO effectively with external parties, such as parents, service providers, and vendors
Communicate effectively both orally and in writing
